jobs.title: Workforce Experience Associate / Specialist
jobs.description: About SuperAnnotate SuperAnnotate is a San Francisco based AI company. We specialize in providing cutting-edge data pipeline solutions for Machine Learning, LLM, and GenAI solutions to large enterprise clients, helping them leverage the power of AI to transform their businesses. SuperAnnotate has a fully customizable platform for building annotation tools and workflows that AI projects demand — while unifying the management of all teams, vendors, and data in one place. We’re very proud to have products that are loved by our customers, resulting in us being listed as the highest-ranked platform on G2 . Why This Role Matters We are seeking a highly detail-oriented Workforce Experience Associate / Specialist to support the execution of complex Large Language Model (LLM) and multimodal annotation projects. As a Workforce Experience Associate / Specialist, you will play a key role in keeping LLM and multimodal annotation projects on track while ensuring contractors remain productive and supported after onboarding. This role bridges AI data operations and contractor success, helping resolve operational, technical, and payment-related issues that can impact delivery and quality. Your work will directly influence on-time delivery, data quality, and contractor experience—critical to scaling AI data pipelines for global enterprise clients. What You Will Do Own and drive the end-to-end execution of complex LLM, multimodal, and annotation workflows, ensuring adherence to project requirements, quality standards, delivery timelines, and operational priorities. Translate project requirements into clear execution strategies, task structures, and actionable guidance for Associates, annotators, and QA specialists, including handling ambiguous guidelines and edge cases. Manage workforce allocation across projects by assigning, prioritizing, and rebalancing tasks based on skill fit, availability, performance trends, delivery constraints, and operational risk. Drive daily operations by monitoring task progress, throughput, quality metrics, and delivery health; proactively identify risks, resolve blockers, and ensure on-time project completion. Serve as a key operational point of contact for Associates, annotators, and QA specialists, providing guidance, clarifications, and execution support. Monitor quality and operational performance, conduct root-cause analysis of systemic issues, identify recurring error patterns, and recommend process improvements and risk mitigation strategies. Escalate complex operational, contractor, and project-related issues to stakeholders with clear context, impact assessment, and proposed resolutions; act as an escalation point for Associates when deeper analysis or cross-functional coordination is required. Manage post-onboarding contractor issues, including execution blockers, platform access, workflow questions, performance concerns, and payment-related inquiries, coordinating with Support, Engineering, Finance, Talent, and other stakeholders to ensure timely resolution. Maintain accurate documentation, reporting, and issue tracking related to project execution, quality outcomes, operational metrics, contractor support, and key learnings. Contribute to the continuous improvement of SOPs, operational playbooks, communication templates, and workflow processes to support scalable and efficient AI data operations. Support and mentor AI Workforce Experience Associates by sharing best practices, providing operational guidance, and assisting with complex issue resolution. Collaborate cross-functionally to build a scalable, reliable, and contractor-friendly AI data operations environment that delivers high-quality outcomes for global enterprise clients. What You Will Bring Educational Background: Bachelor’s degree in any relevant field English proficiency: C2 level (Proficient / Near-Native) required. Experience: 1-3 years Strong understanding of annotation workflows, especially for LLM, NLP, vision-language, or multimodal projects. High proficiency in task tracking using spreadsheets and collaboration tools. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple task streams simultaneously. Proactive problem-solver with a keen eye for operational gaps and execution risks. Experience with Slack, Discord, Jira, or similar collaboration/project tools is a plus. Familiarity with data annotation platforms and QA workflows. A basic understanding of LLM or multimodal AI concepts is a strong advantage. Exposure to scripting or automation (e.g. Python, Sheets formulas) is a plus. Why Join Us? Work on cutting-edge LLM and multimodal AI projects used by global enterprise clients. Gain hands-on exposure to real-world AI data operations at scale. Build strong operational, coordination, and problem-solving skills in a fast-growing AI infrastructure environment. Compensation & Benefits: Competitive salary aligned with experience and company policy. Festival bonuses and performance-based incentives. Learning and professional development opportunities in AI operations. Work Schedule & Location: 24/7 operational environment supporting global AI projects. Location: Mirpur DOHS (Remote and/or Hybrid) Schedule and Shifts: Any 5 working days per week (rostered), which may include weekends based on operational requirements. Rotational shifts aligned with 24/7 operational requirements. Shifts will be assigned based on project needs and team rostering, with advance notice provided. Salary: BDT 35,000 - 50,000 BDT (Based on Skills and Experience) Note : In addition to the monthly salary, employees are eligible for Two Festival Bonuses Earned Leave Encashment Quarterly Performance Bonus Group Health Insurance Yearly Performance and Salary Review Employee Engagement Programs (Pahela Baishakh, Falgun, Year-Ending Program, New Year Celebration, Annual Picnic / Outing) Morning Snacks Our Unique Offers Innovative Environment: Join a top Global AI innovator at the forefront of cutting-edge advancements. Impactful Work: Contribute to global AI progress and shape the future of technology by building our human data engine. Growth Opportunity : Ideal for professionals seeking new challenges in the global AI industry. Competitive Compensation: Enjoy a rewarding salary and a comprehensive benefits package. Multicultural Exposure: Thrive in a diverse collaborative environment that fuels innovation. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview! The job will require to be contracted through our local partner in Bangladesh. Equal Opportunity We are an equal-opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. At SuperAnnotate diversity means to us making an effort to reflect the many experiences and identities of the outside world, and treating each other with fairness and without bias. Every day we foster an environment where people of all backgrounds not only belong, but excel to succeed as a company and grow together. We offer equal opportunity regardless of sex, sexual orientation, national origin, color, race, age, marital status, disability, gender identity, veterans and more. jobs.title: Software Engineer Intern
jobs.description: [Read "How to Apply" First Before Applying] Company: Skarion Type: Full-Time Internship Mode: Remote Duration: 4 Months Working Hours: 9 hours per day including 1 hour lunch break, 5 days a week Compensation: BDT 10,000 per month About Skarion Skarion helps individuals confidently navigate the hiring process and secure better career opportunities through expert coaching, resume optimization, profile grooming, hands-on training, and job placement support. We work closely with candidates to improve their professional positioning, prepare them for the U.S. job market, and support them throughout the journey of landing suitable roles. Our work combines education, career development, technology, automation, and operational execution. Role Overview We are looking for Computer Science graduates to join Skarion as a Software Engineer Intern . This role is ideal for someone who enjoys hands-on development, diving into systems, building new features, and working in a fast-moving startup environment. In this role, you will take ownership of existing projects, maintain active workflows, diagnose and fix bugs, and implement new functionality across our applications and internal tools. We need someone adaptable who isn’t afraid to navigate unfamiliar codebases, improve system reliability, and handle technical tasks across the development lifecycle. Key Responsibilities Project Ownership: Take over, understand, and maintain existing codebases, projects, and active operational workflows. Feature Development: Design, build, and deploy new features and enhancements based on business requirements. Bug Fixing & Maintenance: Identify, troubleshoot, and resolve bugs, performance bottlenecks, and technical glitches across existing applications. System Integration: Integrate and maintain third-party services, REST APIs, and webhooks to ensure smooth data flow across platforms. Code Quality & Optimization: Refactor existing code where necessary to improve readability, maintainability, and reliability. Documentation & Testing: Write clean documentation for systems, workflows, and changes; test updates thoroughly before deployment. Startup Agility: Collaborate directly with the team to translate operational and product needs into practical technical solutions. Required Skills and Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science. Solid grasp of core programming principles, data structures, algorithms, and web technologies. Proficiency in at least one modern language/stack (e.g., JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Node.js). Experience reading, debugging, and navigating existing codebases written by others. Solid understanding of REST APIs, JSON, webhooks, and third-party integrations. Working knowledge of Git and version control workflows (branching, PRs, merge conflict resolution). Basic understanding of relational or NoSQL databases (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB). Strong analytical, debugging, and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail. Good communication skills and self-discipline to work effectively in a remote environment. Preferred Skills Familiarity with modern frontend or full-stack frameworks (e.g., React, Next.js). Experience with backend frameworks and building/consuming internal APIs. Exposure to deploying and managing applications on cloud platforms or VPS (e.g., Vercel, AWS, Render, Docker). Experience working with third-party tools, webhooks, or automation/workflow platforms when integrating backend systems. Familiarity with database schema updates, migrations, and basic query optimization. Prior experience contributing to open-source projects or maintaining production code in an internship/academic project setting. Who we are Looking for We are looking for someone with a startup mindset. This means you should be flexible, curious, resourceful, and willing to work on different types of tasks. You should not expect every task to come with a perfect instruction manual. Sometimes you will need to figure things out, research solutions, test tools, and build practical systems that save time for the team. This role is suitable for someone who wants real-world experience in automation, business operations, API integration, and startup execution. How to Apply Please read this section carefully. Do not apply through LinkedIn or another job platform. To apply, first research Skarion , then email your application directly to: info@skarion.com Following the application instructions is part of our evaluation process. Email Subject Use this exact format: Software Engineer Intern – [Full Name] Examples: Software Engineer Intern – Rahim Ahmed Software Engineer Intern – Nusrat Jahan Software Engineer Intern – Tanvir Hasan Software Engineer Intern – Sadia Akter What to Include in Your Email Please copy the following format and complete it in your email: Full Name: Email: Phone/WhatsApp: Current Location: University: Bachelor’s Degree: Graduation Year: Earliest Start Date: Then answer the following questions: What did you learn about Skarion after researching us? Why are you interested in this internship? Why do you believe you would be a strong fit for our team? What makes you different from other entry-level candidates? Describe one difficult technical topic, tool, or process you taught yourself. Describe a situation where you solved a problem without being given step-by-step instructions. What type of technical work would you most like to learn? What is one area you are currently working to improve? Please answer in your own words. Generic or copied responses will receive lower priority. Required Attachments Please include: Resume in PDF format Degree and university information LinkedIn profile, if available Portfolio, GitHub, project documentation, or other relevant work, if applicable Use a professional email address, and make sure your resume clearly shows your degree and graduation status. How We Evaluate Applications We look at more than grades or previous work experience. We will evaluate: Whether you followed the instructions Written English and communication Academic background Technical curiosity Independent research ability Problem-solving and reasoning Ownership and initiative Reliability and availability Ability to explain technical concepts clearly Professionalism and attention to detail We are trying to understand how you think and how you learn, not simply how many technologies you can list on a resume. A Final Note This internship is probably not a good fit if you want a narrowly defined role where someone provides step-by-step instructions for every task. It may be a strong fit if you want to: Learn quickly and take on unfamiliar problems. Work with a U.S.-based engineering and technology team. Gain exposure to multiple technical disciplines. Take responsibility early in your career. Receive direct feedback and improve from it. Build practical technical and professional experience. Earn the opportunity to move into a full-time role based on performance. If you are curious, disciplined, resourceful, and willing to figure things out, we would like to hear from you. jobs.description: Job Description Tiered Approach In Line With The Commitment To Safeguard Capacity And Support Personnel Already In The Organization, a Majority Of UNDP UNCDF/UNV Vacancies Are Advertised Using a Tiered Application Process Whereby Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026. Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply. Background Bangladesh is the second-largest economy in South Asia, with a gross domestic product (GDP) of over USD 450 billion. Between 2000 and 2019, the economy grew at an average of around 6 per cent per year, accompanied by broad gains in human development. The national poverty rate fell from over 48 per cent in 2000 to about 18.7 per cent in 2022, and the Human Development Index reached 0.685 in 2023, placing Bangladesh in the medium human development category. The country is scheduled to graduate from Least Developed Country (LDC) status in November 2026. Significant development challenges remain. GDP growth slowed to 3.49 per cent in fiscal year 2024–25, inflation has stayed elevated, and private investment is weak, constraining the economic diversification needed to create decent jobs. Bangladesh is also one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries, highly exposed to natural and climate-induced hazards. As the UN’s development agency, UNDP has worked in Bangladesh since 1972, partnering with the government to advance democratic governance, climate adaptation, environmental protection, and inclusive growth. This support spans high-quality policy and technical advice, implementation support, development financing, and knowledge sharing. The programme portfolio is organized into two clusters and a Sub-Office in Cox’s Bazar; Democratic Governance, and Resilience and Inclusive Growth aligned to the Country Programme Document (CPD) and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). Each cluster is led by a Cluster Team Leader (functional title: Assistant Resident Representative) and Sub-Office by its head responsible for programme and project quality, results, and effective relationships with implementing partners and donors. Across both clusters, the Operations Team and the Programme Management Support Unit (PMSU) provide cross-cutting oversight and quality assurance, helping to ensure compliance, delivery readiness, and sound financial and operational management. The Operations Team is a key enabler of programme delivery, ensuring the right systems, resources, and processes are in place for results to happen. Working under the leadership of the Operations Advisor, it covers the full range of operational functions administration, procurement, finance, human resources, ICT, and security and collaborates closely with programme teams, extending operational support to partner UN agencies where needed. Its core focus is compliance with UNDP rules and regulations, effective internal controls, and continuous improvement of operational systems, combining sound process management with responsiveness, anticipation of programme needs, and sound judgment. UNDP Bangladesh delivers a diverse programme portfolio spanning democratic governance, climate and environment, and inclusive growth, including operations in geographically remote and security-sensitive areas such as the Chittagong Hill Tracts and coastal, disaster-prone districts. Programme delivery depends on a functioning security risk management framework that enables personnel, partners and communities to operate safely. The Host Government bears primary responsibility for the safety and security of personnel and property of organizations within the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS). UNDSS holds responsibility for United Nations system security risk management in Bangladesh, including the security risk assessments, the security risk management measures, the country security plan, the Security Operations Centre, the warden system and the issuance of advisories. The Country Office security function, working with the UNDP Security Office, the Regional Security Advisor and the Sub-Regional Security Specialist, and with UNDSS, supports UNDP compliance with that framework; it does not substitute for it. Bangladesh has been undergoing a significant political transition since August 2024. National elections and a constitutional referendum held in February 2026 returned a new elected government. The security risk management situational analyses describe the political climate as cautiously stable but fragile, with law-and-order institutions still being reconstituted and primacy for public order returning to the police and civil authorities. UNDP operations fall within seven security risk management areas. The approved general threat assessments rate crime, civil unrest and hazards as substantial or high in the Dhaka Metro, Cox’s Bazar and Chittagong Hill Tracts areas, and the security level in the Dhaka Metro and Chittagong Hill Tracts areas is 3 (Moderate). Duties And Responsibilities Under the overall security accountability of the Resident Representative and the day-to-day supervision of the Operations Advisor, and under the technical supervision of the Sub-Regional Security Specialist for Asia and the Pacific together with the Regional Security Advisor, the Security Officer provides security risk management support to Country Office management to enable effective UNDP programme delivery throughout Bangladesh, within the framework of the UNSMS and UNDP security policies and procedures. The position prepares, analyses and recommends; decisions carrying operational risk consequences are taken by the Resident Representative, the Deputy Resident Representative or the Operations Advisor. The incumbent will have the following specific duties and responsibilities: Security risk management and programming support Support the preparation of security risk assessments for UNDP programmes, projects and operations across all areas of assignment, including the Chittagong Hill Tracts and other field locations, and recommend mitigation measures for the approval of the Resident Representative or the Operations Advisor. Support the mainstreaming of security, and its costs, into all stages of programme and project design, implementation and delivery, under the technical guidance of the Regional Security Advisor and the Sub-Regional Security Specialist. Analyse the effect of security factors and trends on programme planning and delivery, and the effect of programme design on stability and security and submit recommendations to management. Prepare inputs for UNDSS for the preparation and periodic update of country and area-specific security risk assessments and related documentation. Support application of the Person-Centred Approach in security risk management to address specific threats, risks or vulnerabilities identified through assessments. Security plans, business continuity and compliance with the UN security framework Support the establishment, maintenance and testing of Country Office security and contingency plans in accordance with the UN Security Policy Manual (SPM) and the country-specific Security Risk Management (SRM) process, in coordination with UNDSS. Ensure that all UNDP personnel, including project personnel and eligible dependants, are captured in the Security Plan maintained by UNDSS, working with the Human Resources and Procurement Units to keep personnel and eligible family member lists current. Prepare security-related inputs to the Country Office Business Continuity Plan, aligned with UNDP Business Continuity Management, Enterprise Risk Management and the UN Country Team Business Continuity Plan. Monitor and report on compliance with Security Risk Management Measures (SRMM) and Residential Security Measures (RSM) for UNDP premises, residences, equipment and personnel, through the UNDP corporate Security Compliance Survey (SCS) online tool. Prepare advice for the Resident Representative and the Operations Advisor on funding requirements under the UN Mandated Security Measures mechanism, reflecting the measures identified through the country-specific SRM process. Coordinate fire safety, first aid, security communications and other security-related training for Country Office personnel, in collaboration with UNDSS. Prepare and process security clearance requests for UNDP personnel travelling to restricted or field areas, for approval by the Operations Advisor. Support to Country Office security personnel, briefing and training Provide day-to-day work direction and technical guidance to the Security Assistant based in the Chittagong Hill Tracts. Deliver orientation, briefings and training to UNDP personnel, national and international, on security guidelines, communication procedures, travel precautions and emergency and curfew arrangements, in coordination with the Regional Security Advisor, the Sub-Regional Security Specialist and UNDSS. Ensure that security equipment inventories, communication systems and access control mechanisms are maintained and kept up to date. Identify learning and capacity-building needs of Country Office security personnel and coordinate with the Regional Security Advisor, the Sub-Regional Security Specialist and UNDSS on relevant training opportunities. Incident reporting, information and liaison support and support knowledge sharing Provide timely and accurate security advice and briefings to the Resident Representative, the Deputy Resident Representative, the Operations Advisor, programme and project managers and visiting personnel. Report immediately all security-related incidents involving UNDP personnel and eligible family members to the Resident Representative, the Operations Advisor, the Regional Security Advisor, the Sub-Regional Security Specialist and UNDSS, and support coordinated 24-hour incident response. Support liaison with UNDSS and with security counterparts in other UN agencies. Liaison with national law enforcement, civil authorities and host Government security authorities is conducted through UNDSS or in the company of a designated UNDP staff member. Attend inter-agency security coordination mechanisms, including the Security Cell, the Area Security Management Team and the Security Management Team, in a technical support capacity accompanying the designated UNDP staff member, and prepare the supporting technical inputs and briefing material. Contribute to security-related knowledge networks and professional communities within UNDP and the wider UNSMS. Premises and residential security compliance support Conduct periodic security assessments of UNDP premises, guesthouses, vehicles and equipment, and advise on shortfalls with recommended SRM and RSM measures. Support implementation of physical security and access control measures, including visitor and vehicle screening, for Country Office and project premises. Provide technical support to the designated UNDP staff member on UNDP security requirements in common UN premises, ensuring that the safety and security of personnel remain primary considerations. The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description: Software Engineer | Meridian Review Group Remote, London, Prague or Costa Rica | Full-Time or Long-Term Contract | $9,000–$12,000 per month depending on experience Meridian Review Group is looking for a Software Engineer to join our growing international team and help build the technology behind a rapidly expanding network of independent business, markets and economic publications. This is a role for someone who wants to build, not simply maintain. Meridian currently operates specialist publications covering major economies, financial markets, companies, technology, investment and economic change. Our network includes Global Markets Review, British Business Review, American Commerce Review, German Business Review, Dutch Business Review, Czech Business Review and Gulf Business Review . We are building Meridian as much more than a collection of conventional news websites. Alongside journalism, we are developing market-data products, company and executive databases, rankings, economic datasets, research tools, structured entity systems, internal editorial technology and new ways for readers to understand companies, industries, markets and economies. The role can be fully remote or based from one of our locations in London, Prague or Costa Rica . What We’re Building Meridian Review Group is an international publishing, research and intelligence group covering business, markets, investment, technology, AI, energy, infrastructure, manufacturing, finance and economic policy. Our model combines timely journalism with information designed to remain useful long after publication. That includes: Company and executive profiles Market and stock data Economic and regional guides Industry directories Rankings and indexes Investment trackers Original research datasets Company, sector and geographic databases Searchable reference products Specialist newsletters and recurring editorial products Data-backed journalism Research and intelligence products for professional audiences The network is already reaching a meaningful audience, but we are building the infrastructure with a much larger goal in mind. Our ambition is to create a publishing and information platform capable of reaching millions of readers every month , ultimately building toward 10 million monthly visitors across the Meridian network . We currently reach approximately 480,000 readers across our publications in under a year and are growing rapidly. That creates a very different engineering challenge from building a single publication. We need systems that can support multiple brands, thousands and eventually hundreds of thousands of content and entity pages, rapidly growing search traffic, structured datasets, financial information, new publications and entirely new research products without the platform becoming increasingly difficult to maintain. We want to build systems that work well today while being designed for what Meridian could become several years from now. One Platform, Multiple Publications One of the more interesting parts of the engineering challenge is that Meridian is not one website. Much of the network operates from a shared technical foundation, while each publication maintains its own identity, editorial focus, domain, information architecture and audience. An improvement to the underlying platform might therefore benefit: Global Markets Review British Business Review American Commerce Review German Business Review Dutch Business Review Czech Business Review Gulf Business Review and future Meridian publications that have not yet launched. This creates opportunities to build reusable systems for: Publishing Structured data Company profiles Authors Topics Geographic hubs Market data Rankings Research products Internal linking Search SEO Analytics Advertising Subscriptions Editorial workflows while still allowing each publication to evolve independently. What You’d Work On There isn’t a narrow list of tickets waiting for you. You’ll work with our existing engineering, editorial and leadership teams to determine what we should build next and how we should build it. Depending on your strengths, that could include: Building new reader-facing products and features Improving the shared Meridian publishing platform Building infrastructure that allows us to launch new publications efficiently Creating tools for journalists, editors and researchers Building structured company, executive, industry and economic databases Developing market-data infrastructure Creating stock and company information products Building APIs and data pipelines Integrating external financial and economic datasets Building ranking and index products Developing systems for original Meridian research Improving article discovery and recommendation Building stronger topic, company, sector and geographic architecture Developing search and research functionality Improving technical SEO and Core Web Vitals Building entity-based internal linking systems Developing automated publishing and editorial workflows Creating internal monitoring and intelligence tools Building systems to monitor data freshness and accuracy Automating indexing, canonical, redirect and orphan-page audits Improving analytics and understanding how readers interact with the network Experimenting with AI-assisted research, classification and editorial tooling Building future subscription and premium research products Developing infrastructure for advertisers and commercial products Some projects will be highly visible. Others might remove hours of repetitive editorial work or quietly improve thousands of pages across the network. Both matter. Building for Scale A major part of this role is helping us prepare Meridian for a much larger audience. We want the network to be technically capable of supporting 10 million monthly visitors as the publications grow. This is not simply a traffic problem. Growth means considerably more: Articles Companies Executives Stock pages Geographic pages Industry pages Rankings Datasets Publications APIs Internal relationships between entities Search-engine crawling Data updates Editorial activity That means thinking seriously about: Performance under significantly higher traffic Efficient rendering and caching Database and API performance Infrastructure reliability Search and indexing at very large content volumes Programmatic page generation Cost-efficient scaling Monitoring and observability Content delivery architecture Data freshness Search-engine crawl efficiency Resilience during major market or breaking-news traffic spikes Shared infrastructure across multiple domains Preventing architectural decisions that work for seven publications but become problematic at twenty We do not expect every engineer to arrive having built a 10-million-user publishing platform. We do want people who understand the difference between building something that works and building something that can continue working as usage, data and complexity increase dramatically. Data Is Becoming a Major Part of Meridian Meridian is increasingly building products where journalism and structured information sit alongside one another. Global Markets Review, for example, incorporates company and market information. Across the wider network we are developing products including company databases, executive profiles, economic datasets, investment trackers, rankings and proprietary research. Examples include research and data projects around: AI adoption Corporate leadership Gulf AI and infrastructure investment Companies and markets Regional economies Technology ecosystems Investment Energy and infrastructure We expect this side of Meridian to expand considerably. Some products may begin as datasets used by journalists. Others may become searchable public resources. Some may eventually become subscription or professional intelligence products. Engineering will play a major role in determining how those systems are designed. Building an Entity-Based Publishing Platform One particularly important engineering direction for Meridian is structured information. An article about a company should not exist in isolation. That company might also connect to: Its company profile Executives Stock information Headquarters Countries and cities Industries Competitors Rankings Investment activity Previous Meridian coverage Relevant economic indicators Research datasets The same applies to people, industries, regions and markets. Over time we want Meridian to become increasingly good at understanding and representing those relationships. That creates interesting engineering problems around databases, entity resolution, structured data, search, internal linking, page generation and information architecture. The Kind of Engineer We’re Looking For We’re less interested in finding somebody who matches a rigid technology checklist than somebody who can look at a problem, understand why it matters and work out a sensible way to solve it. You’ll probably enjoy this role if you like a relatively high level of ownership. We’re particularly interested in engineers who: Have built real production software used by real users Are comfortable moving between frontend and backend problems Can understand an unfamiliar codebase quickly Care about performance, reliability and maintainability Think about scale rather than only immediate implementation Understand databases and structured information Enjoy solving ambiguous problems rather than only executing predefined tickets Can explain technical trade-offs to non-engineers Are interested in publishing, markets, research, data or information products Understand that SEO can be an engineering problem as much as a marketing problem Know when a simple solution is better than an elaborate one Are comfortable working asynchronously with an internationally distributed team Like experimenting, but can distinguish useful experimentation from unnecessary complexity Are interested in building systems that may eventually serve millions of users You do not need previous experience working for a newspaper or media organisation. Experience building SaaS products, research platforms, financial products, data products, marketplaces, content systems or startup products could all translate particularly well. Technology Our current environment includes technologies and tools such as: TypeScript JavaScript React Next.js Node.js Git and GitHub Vercel SQL and modern databases REST APIs Structured data Analytics infrastructure Modern web performance tooling Technical SEO systems AI APIs and automation workflows External financial, market and economic datasets Experience across the entire stack is not expected. Strong engineering fundamentals, curiosity and the ability to learn quickly matter considerably more than having every technology on your CV. Engineering Inside a Publishing and Research Group One of the things that makes this role different is the proximity between engineering and the rest of Meridian. You won’t be several layers removed from the people using what you build. An editor might identify a research process that takes several hours and could be automated. A financial dataset might need to update thousands of company pages. A new ranking might require its own methodology, database and publishing architecture. A new Meridian publication might need country, company, topic and city infrastructure before launch. Search data might reveal an entirely new information product worth building. An internal dataset might become valuable enough to turn into a public research platform. We want engineering involved in those conversations early. The best solution may be a new application. Sometimes it might be an API, an automation, a database, an interface or twenty lines of code that eliminate an unnecessary workflow. A Small Team With Real Ownership Meridian remains small enough that individual engineers can have a substantial effect on the product. You won’t be engineer number 400 respons

jobs.title: Project Analyst (Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning) - [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description: Job Description Tiered Approach In Line With The Commitment To Safeguard Capacity And Support Personnel Already In The Organization, a Majority Of UNDP UNCDF/UNV Vacancies Are Advertised Using a Tiered Application Process Whereby Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026. Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply. Background Bangladesh is the second-largest economy in South Asia, with a gross domestic product (GDP) of over USD 450 billion. Between 2000 and 2019, the economy grew at an average of around 6 per cent per year, accompanied by broad gains in human development. The national poverty rate fell from over 48 per cent in 2000 to about 18.7 per cent in 2022, and the Human Development Index reached 0.685 in 2023, placing Bangladesh in the medium human development category. The country is scheduled to graduate from Least Developed Country (LDC) status in November 2026. Significant development challenges remain. GDP growth slowed to 3.49 per cent in fiscal year 2024–25, inflation has stayed elevated, and private investment is weak, constraining the economic diversification needed to create decent jobs. Bangladesh is also one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries, highly exposed to natural and climate-induced hazards. As the UN’s development agency, UNDP has worked in Bangladesh since 1972, partnering with the government to advance democratic governance, climate adaptation, environmental protection, and inclusive growth. This support spans high-quality policy and technical advice, implementation support, development financing, and knowledge sharing. The programme portfolio is organized into two clusters and a Sub-Office in Cox’s Bazar; Democratic Governance, and Resilience and Inclusive Growth aligned to the Country Programme Document (CPD) and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). Each cluster is led by a Cluster Team Leader (functional title: Assistant Resident Representative) and Sub-Office by its head responsible for programme and project quality, results, and effective relationships with implementing partners and donors. Across both clusters, the Operations Team and the Programme Management Support Unit (PMSU) provide cross-cutting oversight and quality assurance, helping to ensure compliance, delivery readiness, and sound financial and operational management. UNDP Bangladesh’s Democratic Governance programme works toward a country that is inclusive, capable, rule-based, accountable, and transparent, so that all citizens can contribute peacefully to national development. It focuses on three areas: strengthening effective and accountable governance that improves equitable access to justice and the rule of law; promoting participatory governance and a strong civil society so that all voices are heard; and advancing the civic, political, and economic empowerment of women and youth. In practice, this work spans support to justice-sector institutions and access to justice including legal aid and community-based dispute resolution such as the Village Courts alongside strengthening local government institutions and decentralized service delivery, advancing human rights, transparency, and anti-corruption, and supporting inclusive, credible electoral processes. UNDP partners with government, civil society, community, and academic institutions to make public institutions more effective, accountable, and responsive, with particular attention to women, youth, and marginalized and minority groups. The Social Security Policy Support (SSPS) Phase II (2026–2030), implemented by UNDP Bangladesh in partnership with the Government of Bangladesh and the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) of Australia, supports the implementation and continued reform of the National Social Security Strategy (NSSS). Building on more than a decade of engagement, the programme addresses persistent challenges in Bangladesh’s social protection system, including fragmented delivery, coverage and targeting gaps, limited gender responsiveness, and uneven implementation capacity, particularly at the local level. The programme focuses on strengthening social protection governance and delivery systems, with particular attention to lifecycle-based support for poor and vulnerable populations. Through embedded technical assistance, government-led pilots, improved data and monitoring systems, and evidence-based policy support, SSPS Phase II will advance reforms in governance and local delivery, lifecycle social protection, climate-responsive and shock-adaptive social protection, urban and social insurance linkages, and gender equality and disability inclusion. The programme aims to translate policy commitments into effective, inclusive, and fiscally sustainable social protection that contributes to poverty reduction, human development, employment, and resilience. Duties And Responsibilities She/he will have the following specific duties and responsibilities: 1- Lead Project Monitoring, Evaluation, Results Reporting and Adaptive Learning: Lead the design, implementation and periodic review of the Project MEL Plan, Results Framework, indicators, monitoring tools, performance tracking systems and reporting templates. Coordinate monitoring of programme outputs, outcomes, indicators and milestones across the programme’s thematic portfolios, ensuring timely collection, verification, analysis and reporting of quantitative and qualitative data. Conduct and coordinate data quality assessments and maintain robust monitoring databases and performance information to support results-based management and decision-making. Coordinate preparation of Results-Oriented Annual Reports (ROAR), DFAT and other donor reports, annual and periodic progress reports, and other corporate reporting requirements. Coordinate project evaluations, reviews and assessments, including preparation and follow-up of management responses and implementation of evaluation recommendations. Produce and coordinate analytical reports, lessons learned, case studies, outcome stories and other evidence products, and facilitate reflection and learning processes to support adaptive programme management and policy dialogue. Provide substantive MEL inputs to technical documents, policy papers, concept notes, research, evaluations and programme design, and strengthen feedback loops between evidence, implementation and management decision-making. Provide technical guidance to project personnel and government counterparts on the effective use and administration of dashboards, digital MEL systems and related information platforms for monitoring, reporting and evidence-based decision-making. 2- Strengthen Evidence Generation, Data Analytics and Digital MEL Systems: Lead the administration, maintenance, enhancement and continuous development of the NSSS M&E Dashboard, NSSS Reform Tracking Dashboard and related digital monitoring and evidence systems in response to evolving social protection policies, programmes and information needs. Provide technical oversight for digital monitoring, reporting and evidence systems, including integration of monitoring data with the Single Registry MIS, government MIS, mobile applications and other interoperable platforms, to support timely, accurate and accessible programme performance information. Coordinate development and enhancement of digital monitoring architecture that connects national, sub-national and local-level social protection data and supports effective local-to-national evidence and feedback loops. Promote data governance, data quality, interoperability, information security and appropriate data protection measures across digital MEL systems and evidence platforms. Apply data analytics and visualization approaches to transform programme, administrative and other relevant data into dashboards, analytical outputs and decision-support information 3- Support Pilot Monitoring, Household Well-being Evidence Generation and Adaptive Learning: Coordinate monitoring and documentation of SSPS programme pilots, ensuring that implementation experience, results, beneficiary-level data and lessons are systematically incorporated into the project MEL system and used for programme improvement. Support mechanisms for capturing, tracking, analysing and reporting grievances and beneficiary feedback, and strengthen the integration of Grievance Redress System (GRS) evidence into monitoring, reporting and learning processes. Analyse local-level, pilot and beneficiary data to identify implementation and service-delivery gaps, inclusion and exclusion issues, targeting challenges and opportunities for institutionalization or scale-up. Support the SSPS policy and MEL interface for the Bangladesh Multidimensional Household Well-being Panel Survey, working with BBS, Cabinet Division, GED and other relevant stakeholders to articulate policy questions and use cases and ensure that survey evidence responds to social protection reform and programme learning needs. Support the use of survey and other pilot evidence for SDG localization, Family Card learning, social protection targeting and programme performance analysis, and development of decision-oriented evidence products and recommendations. Contribute, within the agreed institutional division of responsibilities, to joint technical processes relating to indicator frameworks, data access, privacy and ethics, analysis and publication planning, and methods review and learning. Translate evidence from pilots, beneficiary feedback and the household well-being survey into recommendations, analytical products and learning that support programme adaptation, policy dialogue and potential scale-up. 4- Lead Digital Knowledge, Evidence Platforms And Technology-Enabled Learning Lead the administration, maintenance, security, enhancement and continuous development of the National Website on Social Protection and related digital evidence platforms to support access to monitoring findings, research, dashboards, learning products and social protection knowledge. Administer the WordPress-based content management system, including user and publishing workflows, system performance, backups, security and other functions necessary for reliable operation of the platform. Coordinate with government counterparts, technical experts and project teams to publish and disseminate policy documents, research, dashboards, knowledge products and other programme evidence through relevant digital platforms. Develop and integrate website functionalities and linkages with project dashboards, monitoring systems, mobile applications and other digital knowledge and evidence platforms to improve accessibility and use of programme evidence. Monitor platform usage and analytics and use findings to strengthen access to and dissemination of monitoring evidence, research and programme learning. Support technology-enabled programme learning, knowledge-sharing and evidence-dissemination events through appropriate digital tools, including digital registration, QR-based attendance, electronic feedback, digital materials, presentation and information-sharing systems, ensuring that relevant participation and feedback data contribute to programme learning and knowledge management. 5- Coordinate MEL, Evidence Use and Reporting with Government and Partners: Coordinate with the Cabinet Division, General Economics Division, BBS, relevant ministries

Distributed systems: Event-driven systems, messaging, asynchronous processing, workflow orchestration and resilient services. Data engineering: Data pipelines, transformation, storage, search, data quality and analytical platforms. Cloud and DevOps engineering: Infrastructure, containers, CI/CD, deployment automation, observability, security and operational reliability. Understanding of common agentic patterns, including workflow orchestration, routing, state management and human oversight. Familiarity with retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings, semantic search or knowledge-grounded systems. Ability to assess when AI is appropriate and when conventional software or rules would be safer and more effective. Awareness of common AI application risks, including hallucination, prompt injection, unsafe tool use and unintended data exposure. Understanding of how to evaluate and improve AI application quality rather than relying solely on subjective demonstrations. Experience with frameworks such as LangGraph, LangChain, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen or similar platforms is helpful, but we value sound engineering judgement over familiarity with any particular framework. jobs.description: Company Description TigerIT Bangladesh Ltd. designs and delivers end-to-end identity and credential management solutions for government, corporate, healthcare, and other large-scale service providers worldwide. The company’s flagship Automated Fingerprint Identification System, TigerAFIS, is NIST-certified and ranked among the top global biometric solutions. TigerIT’s portfolio includes biometric enrollment, card and identity document management, inventory management, and e-business solutions used for national IDs, e-passports, border control, criminal identification, and smart card driver’s licenses. jobs.title: Project Manager (Open to Internal & External Applicants)
jobs.description: Job Description Tiered Approach In Line With The Commitment To Safeguard Capacity And Support Personnel Already In The Organization, a Majority Of UNDP UNCDF/UNV Vacancies Are Advertised Using a Tiered Application Process Whereby Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026. Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply. Background Office/Unit/Project Description Bangladesh is the second-largest economy in South Asia, with a gross domestic product (GDP) of over USD 450 billion. Between 2000 and 2019, the economy grew at an average of around 6 per cent per year, accompanied by broad gains in human development. The national poverty rate fell from over 48 per cent in 2000 to about 18.7 per cent in 2022, and the Human Development Index reached 0.685 in 2023, placing Bangladesh in the medium human development category. The country is scheduled to graduate from Least Developed Country (LDC) status in November 2026. Significant development challenges remain. GDP growth slowed to 3.49 per cent in fiscal year 2024–25, inflation has stayed elevated, and private investment is weak, constraining the economic diversification needed to create decent jobs. Bangladesh is also one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries, highly exposed to natural and climate-induced hazards. As the UN’s development agency, UNDP has worked in Bangladesh since 1972, partnering with the government to advance democratic governance, climate adaptation, environmental protection, and inclusive growth. This support spans high-quality policy and technical advice, implementation support, development financing, and knowledge sharing. The programme portfolio is organized into two clusters and a Sub-Office in Cox’s Bazar; Democratic Governance, and Resilience and Inclusive Growth aligned to the Country Programme Document (CPD) and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). Each cluster is led by a Cluster Team Leader (functional title: Assistant Resident Representative) and Sub-Office by its head responsible for programme and project quality, results, and effective relationships with implementing partners and donors. Across both clusters, the Operations Team and the Programme Management Support Unit (PMSU) provide cross-cutting oversight and quality assurance, helping to ensure compliance, delivery readiness, and sound financial and operational management. UNDP has been a long-standing partner of the Government of Bangladesh on economic development and on nature, climate, and energy. The RIG Cluster leads programming and policy advice on inclusive and sustainable economic development and on a sustainable, resilient, and healthy environment. It supports the country through policy and technical advice, implementation support, resource mobilization and development financing, capacity development, innovation, knowledge management, and south-south and triangular cooperation. On the economic side, this includes support for inclusive and diversified growth, livelihoods, financial inclusion, and inclusive insurance and risk finance. On the environmental side, it covers climate change adaptation and mitigation, disaster risk reduction, natural-resource and biodiversity management, energy efficiency and renewable energy, and access to climate finance helping Bangladesh reduce greenhouse-gas emissions, manage its natural resources, and build resilience to climate change, including through locally led adaptation that reaches the most climate-vulnerable communities. This position is based within the RIG cluster and will lead and manage two projects related to climate and sustainable finance. These will include the regional i) Climate Finance Network (CFN) Project supported by the FCDO for financing solutions for climate adaptation and ii) upcoming Sweeden-supported Strengthening Thematic Bonds Ecosystem in Bangladesh (TBE) project with a focus on regions, communities and sectors most at climate risks. Scope of Work: The Project Manager at NPSA-10 level will be responsible for the strategic and adaptive leadership of project management, ensuring results-based planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and reporting in line with UNDP's programming principles, the project document, donor requirements and GoB priorities. 3.1 Ensure Results-based Project Management, Planning, Implementation, Monitoring and Evaluation Provide overall management oversight to ensure project implementation is on track and in line with the project document, approved Annual Work Plan (AWP) and results framework. Manage financial and human resources with accountability to the Project Board / Project Steering Committee (PSC) and UNDP, ensuring full compliance with UNDP's financial rules and regulations. Lead the preparation of annual work plans, budgets, procurement plans and operational plans; oversee timely and quality implementation. Manage the project team to ensure a clear division of labour, setting of specific quarterly and annual targets for all personnel, including performance planning and evaluation. Manage risks and issues; execute adaptive management in consultation with the Programme Analyst and the ARR/Cluster Lead. Ensure project quality assurance processes (Social and Environment Screening, audits, spot checks, private sector due diligence etc.) are executed to the highest standards. Champion UNDP’s zero-tolerance standards on sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), sexual harassment and fraud; ensure social and environmental safeguards, duty of care and accountability-to-affected-populations measures are embedded across the project. Prepare and ensure timely submission of high quality monthly, quarterly and annual progress reports, donor reports, Project Implementation Reports (PIR), FACE forms and other reporting as required. Facilitate the functioning of the Project Board/PSC and other governance mechanisms; provide secretariat support including convening meetings, preparing documentation and circulating notes and decisions. Oversee procurement of goods and services; finalize Terms of Reference for consultants and service providers; coordinate with UNDP Operations on recruitment and contracting. Ensure project records, asset registers and documentation are maintained to the required standards. Facilitate government, donor and UNDP regional/HQ field missions and reviews as applicable. 2.2 Provide Technical Oversight, Quality Assurance and Partnership Management Provide technical oversight on climate finance, blended finance, thematic bonds and innovative financing approaches and quality assurance across all project outputs; review and contribute to all outputs and deliverables. Identify stakeholders and implementation partners; develop and implement a stakeholder engagement and partnership strategy. Establish and maintain strategic relationships with Government counterparts (central and local), UN agencies, civil society organizations, the private sector and development partners. Support government institutions, regulators, financial institutions, capital market intermediaries and development partners in strengthening sustainable finance frameworks, climate finance governance systems and market-based financing approaches for climate adaptation and resilient development. Facilitate technical dialogue on sustainable finance taxonomies, climate finance methodologies, disclosure frameworks, and impact measurement systems as relevant to project implementation. Promote approaches that strengthen access to financial services for climate-vulnerable populations, women-led enterprises, MSMEs and underserved communities through inclusive and gender-responsive financing mechanisms. Supervise and guide the work of consultants, experts and service providers; oversee compliance with agreed work plans and deliverables. Ensure that the project draws from and collaborates with other UNDP programmes and portfolios, avoiding duplication and maximizing synergies. Promote integration of cross-cutting themes including gender equality, social inclusion, disability, climate resilience and human rights-based approaches in all project activities. Introduce and maintain feedback mechanisms and open communication channels to ensure that the needs of target groups are reflected in project planning and implementation. 2.3 Provide Evidence-based Advocacy, Policy Support and Stakeholder Engagement Analyse and consolidate project results and provide results-based reporting at outcome and impact levels. Lead capacity development activities targeted at government counterparts, civil society, financial institutions, private sector and other relevant stakeholders. Provide technical and policy advisory inputs to government partners, financial institutions and other relevant stakeholders on thematic areas covered by the project. Participate in inter-agency coordination mechanisms, technical working groups and high-level policy dialogues. Coordinate with relevant development partners and donors on issues related to the project; liaise with government focal persons for smooth coordination. Contribute to national policy processes, action plans and reform initiatives relevant to the project's thematic areas. 2.4 Facilitate Knowledge Management, Communications and Learning Manage and contribute to the development of high-quality knowledge products; ensure effective integration with other practice areas. Lead knowledge creation and dissemination related to national, regional and global know-how in the subject area. Manage the synthesis and documentation of project results, lessons learned, good practices and case studies. Establish and manage internal/external networks or communities of practice covering relevant practitioners and experts. Ensure project results and impact are captured, recorded and shared in knowledge products and communication materials. Prepare and update project information and results on UNDP, government and other platforms on a regular basis. 2.5 Support Resource Mobilization and Donor Relations Mobilize and network with experts of national and regional offices of the UN system, international development organizations, multilateral development banks and the private sector. Identify funding sources and prepare proposals, concept notes, business cases and donor briefings for resource mobilization. Lead the design of diversified and innovative financing strategies – spanning international financial institutions, climate and development finance, vertical funds, the private sector and South-South and triangular cooperation to sustain and scale results in a constrained and evolving ODA environment. Plan, strategize and manage the scaling up of project approaches and results with close guidance from the National Project Director (NPD) and UNDP Country Office. Maintain effective relationships with development partners to facilitate and support resource mobilization efforts. Identify and pursue opportunities for blended finance, climate finance, thematic bonds, sustainable finance instruments and partnerships with development finance institutions, financial sector actors and private investors to support programme objectives and scaling of results. The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. You will evaluate annotations such as bounding boxes, segmentation masks, polygons, keypoints, object classes, attributes, and video tracks, identifying missing, incorrect, inconsistent, or poorly placed annotations. This role requires strong attention to detail, consistency, and the ability to carefully follow detailed computer vision annotation guidelines. Key Responsibilities Review annotation quality: Review image and video annotations for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and adherence to project guidelines. Check annotation outputs: Evaluate bounding boxes, classes, attributes, segmentation masks, polygons, keypoints, image labels, and video tracking outputs. Identify annotation errors: Spot missing objects, incorrect labels, inaccurate boundaries, poor box placement, inconsistent attributes, duplicate annotations, and unclear edge cases. Make corrections when required: Correct annotation issues according to project-specific instructions and quality standards. Provide clear feedback: Document quality issues clearly so annotators or project teams can understand what needs to be improved. Follow project guidelines: Apply detailed annotation rules consistently across tasks, including rules for occlusion, truncation, blur, small objects, overlapping objects, and ambiguous cases. Escalate unclear cases: Communicate questions or uncertain examples to the project team for clarification. Maintain consistent work quality: Complete assigned QA work reliably while maintaining accuracy, consistency, and expected productivity. Your Profile Previous experience with computer vision annotation, image annotation, video annotation, or annotation QA is preferred. Experience reviewing or creating annotations such as bounding boxes, polygons, segmentation masks, keypoints, object classes, attributes, image classification, or video object tracking. Strong attention to detail and ability to identify missing, incorrect, inconsistent, overlapping, mislabeled, or poorly placed annotations. Comfortable working with detailed annotation guidelines, edge-case rules, quality standards, and project-specific instructions. jobs.title: Software Quality Assurance Engineer
jobs.description: About the Company Finding the right job or the right candidate should not take days of searching, repeated form-filling, and guesswork. Nextjobz is building a smarter career platform for Bangladesh where qualified job seekers can discover and apply for the right opportunities quickly, and employers can find suitable candidates with less effort. From AI-assisted profile creation and job matching to faster job posting and candidate recommendations, we are designing every experience around one goal: making career and hiring decisions simpler. We want Nextjobz to feel like a trusted Digital Boro Bhai: practical, dependable, and genuinely committed to helping people move forward in their careers. But smart features only create value when people can trust them to work. A broken application flow can cost someone an opportunity. An incorrect candidate recommendation can waste a recruiter’s time. That is why quality is not just the final step of our development process. It is part of the product itself. About the Role We are looking for a Software Quality Assurance Engineer who cares about the details users notice and the problems they should never have to face. As a Software Quality Assurance Engineer at Nextjobz, you will help ensure that our candidate, employer, and internal products are reliable, accurate, secure, and easy to use. This is a hands-on role combining strong manual testing with practical test automation. You will work closely with product, designers, developers, and other stakeholders throughout the product lifecycle, from reviewing requirements to validating releases in production. You will help us automate critical test scenarios and continuously improve our overall quality process. Responsibilities Review product requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and designs to identify gaps before development begins. Prepare and maintain test plans, test scenarios, test cases, checklists, and test data. Perform functional, regression, integration, system, usability, exploratory, responsive, and cross-browser testing. Test web applications, APIs, databases, and end-to-end user journeys. Build and maintain automated tests for critical workflows. Validate REST APIs using Postman or similar tools. Verify application data using SQL queries and database checks. Identify, document, prioritize, and track defects with clear reproduction steps, supporting evidence, severity, and expected results. Collaborate with developers to investigate issues and verify fixes. Perform smoke testing, release validation, and post-release production checks. Identify edge cases, business-rule conflicts, and potential user-experience problems. Monitor recurring defects and recommend improvements to prevent them. Help increase automation coverage and improve release confidence. Contribute to basic performance, security, accessibility, and compatibility testing. Represent the user’s perspective during product and technical discussions. Qualifications 2–4 years of professional experience in Software Quality Assurance or Software Testing. Strong understanding of testing principles, QA processes, and the software development lifecycle. Solid experience with manual testing of web-based products. Practical experience with functional, regression, integration, exploratory, and usability testing. Hands-on experience with at least one automation framework, such as Playwright, Selenium, or Cypress. Experience testing REST APIs using Postman or an equivalent tool. Working knowledge of SQL and database validation. Ability to write clear, structured, and maintainable test cases. Ability to report bugs with precise reproduction steps and supporting evidence. Understanding of Agile or Scrum-based product development. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities. Good written and verbal communication skills. Ability to take ownership while collaborating effectively with a cross-functional team. Preferred Skills Experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, C#, Java, or another automation-friendly programming language. Familiarity with Git and CI/CD pipelines. Experience with performance-testing tools such as JMeter or k6. Basic understanding of application security and accessibility testing. Experience testing AI-powered features, matching systems, SaaS platforms, marketplaces, or recruitment products. Familiarity with GitLab, Jira, Azure DevOps, or similar tools. Experience testing mobile-responsive products across different devices and browsers.
